summary: Added Loaded event handler to ProvisioningToolsView parameterless constructor: calls StartAsync() on the view-model and subscribes vm.Log.CollectionChanged to OnLogChanged for auto-scroll.
Implemented OnLogChanged: posts a Dispatcher.UIThread.Post that sets LogScrollViewer.Offset.Y = double.MaxValue (Avalonia clamps to maximum scroll).

Updated ProvisioningToolsView.axaml: added Message TextBlock (IsNotNullOrEmpty visibility), wrapped ProgressBar in a two-column Grid with DownloadPercent TextBlock, added bordered ScrollViewer (x:Name=LogScrollViewer, MaxHeight=200) containing an ItemsControl bound to Log.
Build: 0 errors, 0 warnings. Tests: 344 passed, 0 failed.

comments.note: The `OnLogChanged` subscription added in the Loaded handler is never unsubscribed. For this view the DataContext is set once and the view is never detached while `Log` is live, so the lifetime is correct. If re-use patterns change in future, consider unsubscribing in OnDetachedFromVisualTree to avoid a memory leak.

summary: WP-006 passes code review. AXAML and code-behind are clean, minimal, and idiomatic.
All 5 ACs met and previously verified by QA.

AXAML uses compiled bindings correctly (x:DataType set, all bindings type-correct). DownloadPercent label correctly placed in auto-column Grid. Message TextBlock correctly conditioned on IsNotNullOrEmpty. Log panel uses correct MaxHeight and auto-scrolls via Offset=Vector(X,MaxValue).

Code-behind Loaded handler: DataContext type-guard is correct. CollectionChanged subscription before StartAsync call ensures no log entries are missed. Fire-and-forget StartAsync() is safe in void lambda (no CS4014 in non-async context, confirmed by TreatWarningsAsErrors build succeeding).
CollectionChanged subscription without Unloaded cleanup is a deliberate, correct design decision: view and VM have identical lifetimes via the shell state machine's dispose-on-transition contract.
No Fix-Forward edits applied. One low-priority documentation-forward comment raised for the subscription lifetime rationale.

comments.note: No blocking or fix-forward issues found. AXAML uses compiled bindings (x:DataType present), all Binding expressions are correct for their source types, and the auto-scroll idiom (Offset = new Vector(X, MaxValue)) is the standard Avalonia pattern.

Fire-and-forget `vm.StartAsync()` in the Loaded lambda is correct. CS4014 is only emitted in async contexts — the void event handler lambda is non-async, so the compiler does not warn. This is safe with TreatWarningsAsErrors=true.

CollectionChanged subscription without Unloaded cleanup is an intentional, safe design choice. ProvisioningToolsView is constructed once per shell state entry and disposed via IDisposable when the state transitions away (shell calls Dispose on the outgoing view-model). The view and its Log have identical lifetimes, so no memory leak exists.

[documentation-forward] ProvisioningToolsView.axaml.cs would benefit from a brief code comment above the `vm.Log.CollectionChanged += OnLogChanged` line explaining why no Unloaded unsubscription is needed (view lifetime is identical to the VM lifetime via the shell state machine's dispose-on-transition contract). This prevents future maintainers from adding an unnecessary Unloaded handler.
